metadata.description: Ground truth for 4 residual top-level workloads. Each observation is point-in-time: deleted_state is post-Cycle-B (operators absent), recovered_state is post-Ansible-recovery (operators present).

residuals.name: postgres
residuals.gap_explanation: In keycloak namespace (rhbk-operator footprint via plan actions), scanned and found, but no ownerRef/label evidence links it to rhbk-operator → classified UNATTRIBUTED

recovered_state_observation.note: UID changed: keycloak postgres was deleted+PVC cleaned for recovery (stale credentials). Ansible recreated fresh. No ownerRef in either state.

residuals.notes: Created by Ansible, not by rhbk-operator. No ownerRef in any observed state. Ansible deploys it as a standalone postgres for Keycloak.

residuals.name: model-catalog
residuals.gap_explanation: rhoai-model-registries namespace not in any operator's footprint_namespaces (built from install_namespace + plan action namespaces at journal.rs:738-774). Post-delete, ownerRef is absent (mechanism not captured). audit.rs:823 iterates footprint_namespaces only → namespace never scanned → never reported.

deleted_state_observation.note: ownerRef absent after teardown; present after recovery. The mechanism that removed it was not captured.

recovered_state_observation.note: Same UID. ownerRef present after recovery, absent after teardown. The mechanism that removed/re-added it was not captured.

residuals.notes: Created by model-registry-operator (RHOAI sub-component) in cross-namespace pattern. ownerRef to ModelRegistry observed after recovery but absent after teardown; removal/re-addition mechanism not captured. DSC spec.components.modelregistry.registriesNamespace = rhoai-model-registries provides the namespace provenance link.
